question: Is the PlayCover failure primarily driven by the macOS /Users/.../Saved/Paks path class, or do we still need to tighten the explanation to pre-1c8 caller/helper state?

matrix.notes: Real device accepts an absolute Saved/Paks class, so the problem is not the idea of absolute paths by itself.
Real device also accepts the UE4 relative pak class.
This is the PlayCover success control sample documented in HOK-016-C.2.7.
This is the only stable failing path class in the combined evidence set.

findings: Across the combined evidence set, only the macOS /Users/.../Saved/Paks/... class fails stably.
The real-device acceptance of /var/mobile/.../Saved/Paks/... proves that the failure is not caused by absolute-path semantics in general.

PlayCover success and fail hits share the same target identity and converge to the same post-1c8 pointer pair, so the remaining mechanism-level split lives in pre-1c8 compare and caller/helper state rather than in target identity.
For fix-direction choice, path class is a sufficient operational discriminator; for full mechanism closure, pre-1c8 caller/helper state remains residual uncertainty.

decision.b1Conclusion: B1 closes enough evidence to stop treating additional sampling as the default next step.
decision.primaryFixDirection: bundle-scoped ios-semantic path remap / normalization for /Users/.../Saved/Paks/...
decision.whyNotB2Now: The current matrix already isolates a single stable failing path class and a consistent caller-side failure semantic. Extra sampling should be conditional on the remap failing or leaving a new gap.
decision.residualUncertainty: The failing PlayCover hit still carries a distinct pre-1c8 caller/helper state, so the matrix does not prove that path text alone is the sole mechanistic cause.
